model_assumption: For every message m, sum_t x_t(m)^2 <= n P. The constraint is block-average but holds for each codeword, not only after averaging over messages.
For every message m, sum_t sum_k x_{t,k}(m)^2 <= n P. This is a shared transmit-antenna budget for each codeword, not a separate per-antenna or message-averaged budget.
For user j and every local message m_j, sum_t x_{j,t}(m_j)^2 <= n P_j. There is no averaging over messages and no feedback.
For every pair (m_1,m_2), sum_t x_t(m_1,m_2)^2 <= n P. The constraint is not merely an expectation over the message pair.
For every message m and every private seed s, sum_t x_t(m,s)^2 <= n P. This constraint is not averaged over the message or the seed.
For every message m, E_{S^n}[sum_t x_t(m,S^n)^2] <= n P. Energy is integrable under the iid state law. The bound is not pathwise in the state and is not averaged over messages.

E_{M,Z^n}[sum_t x_t(M,Y^{t-1})^2] <= n P, with M uniform and independent of the Gaussian noise. Each message-conditional energy is integrable. This is an expected block-power bound, not a pathwise bound on feedback realizations.

For each user j, E_{M_1,M_2,Z^n}[sum_t x_{j,t}(M_j,Y^{t-1})^2] <= n P_j. The messages are independent and uniform. Every message-pair-conditional energy is integrable. The power bounds are separate and not pathwise.
For every message m, sum_t x_t(m)^2 <= n P. Inputs do not depend on the fading gains. There is no gain-dependent power adaptation or averaging of the power constraint over gains.
For every message m and time t, |x_t(m)| <= A. This is a pathwise peak-amplitude bound, not an average-power constraint.
